 Match Preview 
 Go Media Stadium, Auckland
Saturday, November 21st, 5:00pm NZT 
 Written by Jonno Ross 
 Auckland FC return to Go Media Stadium this Saturday afternoon, welcoming Melbourne Victory, for what promises to be an exciting A-League clash. Our boys are looking to build some consistency early in the campaign, and three points at The Fortress would be a massive result. Can the boys in black and blue get the job done? 
 Auckland will be looking to turn their recent draws into victories after a mixed start to the season. Having just won once in the season opener, Pedro and his side will be hungry to build on their previous two draws, and not only get the three points, but to demonstrate the new head coach’s football philosophy on the pitch. 
 It’s fair to say that Auckland FC were slight underdogs for the New Zealand derby against Wellington Phoenix in their last outing. The Phoenix were off to a flyer at the start of the season, coming into the game undefeated and on top of the A League ladder. Auckland, on the other hand, were looking shaky, and for the first time in the club’s short history, it looked like the Phoenix could come away with their first victory against us.
 Despite a fantastic atmosphere at Go Media Stadium, and chances falling for the home side, neither side could find the breakthrough, with the match finishing 0-0. Pedro Morreira labelled the end result as being “unfair”, feeling that his side should have won the match. Based on how the Yellow Fever were celebrating the 0-0 result, it’s safe to say they felt like they were the winners on the day, picking up their first ever point against their rivals. 
 While Auckland have shown plenty of promise since their 5-2 defeat away at Western Sydney, they’ll know the importance of turning performances into three points. Sitting on five points from their opening four matches, Saturday presents a great opportunity to climb the ladder and build some momentum.
 Melbourne Victory arrive in Auckland also searching for their first league victory of the campaign. Under head coach Giovanni Savarese, Victory have drawn three of their opening four matches, including a 2-2 result against Adelaide United in their most recent outing.
 They’ve shown glimpses of quality but are still searching for consistency. With a club of Victory’s size and expectations, they’ll be desperate to get their season moving in the right direction. Auckland certainly won’t be taking them lightly.
 The biggest challenge for Auckland, will be breaking down Victory’s defence while remaining disciplined at the other end. Auckland have shown cracks in their defence, but their first clean sheet of the season last time out, is a promising sign things are improving. 
 Home advantage could also prove crucial. The Auckland supporters have created some fantastic atmospheres at Go Media Stadium, and another strong turnout could provide the extra motivation needed to get over the line.
 For Pedro Moreira’s men, the message is simple: three points are the priority. A victory against one of the competition’s biggest clubs would be a fantastic confidence boost and exactly what Auckland need to kick-start their campaign.
 Let’s make it a big afternoon at Go Media Stadium.
 Come on Auckland!  🔵⚫️
 PLAYERS TO WATCH  
 Auckland FC – Lachie Bayliss 
 Lachie Bayliss enjoyed the international window with the All Whites. In his side’s 5-0 victory over India, he scored a cracking volley into the right side of the net. Let’s hope he carries that form into Saturday’s match.
 Melbourne Victory – Guillermo May 
 Guillermo May returns to his old stomping ground for the first time since his departure from Auckland FC. Whilst some fans have mixed feelings about his departure to a rival club, he’ll forever be a club legend for what he helped us achieve in the past two seasons. Let’s be sure to welcome him back, but let’s hope he doesn’t enjoy his return too much.
 FUN AT GO MEDIA STADIUM 
 It’s Superhero round at Go Media Stadium this week! 
 There will be superheroes roaming the ground all afternoon as well as princesses and fairies. 
 Come dressed as your favourite superhero – and be in the draw to win best dressed for the day!
 A helicopter is landing on the pitch to deliver the match ball!
 There will be a vertical bungee on site, test your wits and have a go!
 The Maccas football pitch is up and running. Bring the kids along and let them blow off some steam before settling in to watch the match.
 Save the inconvenience of having to drive to the game and make a day of it. Public transport is free!
 There’s 20% off all online merch. This is only for game day so get in quick!
